summary.intent: Cut over-engineering in the Callisto release/CI tooling: decide what to do about the check-api-on-every-pr guard and brittle shell scripts, plan a Rust `release-pr apply` command to replace shell, then start the docs and specs alignment PR.
summary.outcome: Closed PR #453 and deleted its branch, wrote a design doc for `callisto release-pr apply`/`hold`, and committed and pushed a docs/specs/messages alignment branch (docs/align-with-code) with a changeset. Tests, clippy, rustdoc and workflow checks passed; the PR itself was not opened in the transcript.

repo: Architecture doc docs/architecture/release.md says workflow shell must not reimplement Callisto semantics; policy lives in Rust (`release-pr verify`, `decide`, `commit-plan`) and the shell only does forge I/O.

Shell is about 3,600 lines vs 117k lines of Rust; shell tests are about 2,650 lines (3.5x the code they test), including a 615-line stub-based contract test. Stub/fake-tool tests previously hid the 0.10.1 gh regression.
Rust already calls `gh` via the `CommandRunner` seam in callisto-graph (`forge.rs`, `artifact.rs`), so a Rust release-pr apply can reuse it with no new dependencies.
`callisto init` fails with E190 when callisto.toml already exists, so advice to run it to reconcile napi group drift was wrong; fixed to say edit callisto.toml.
Before 1.0, breaking a public Rust item needs a `minor` changeset or `just check-api` fails on the release PR; `check-api` runs only on the release PR.
Several checks run only in CI: hygiene recipes (machete, features-boundary, check-api), per-crate coverage, MSRV, changeset validation, artifact preflight.
Release-workflow plan/build-python/execute jobs check out `github.sha` (detached HEAD) because the release commands require it (E170).
The release-PR flow in the shell script hard-codes `schemaVersion: 2` in jq when building the snapshot (noted in wire-compat.md:27); a wire shape owned by the wrong layer.

code.finding: Notes that the shell builds the release-PR snapshot with a hard-coded schemaVersion: 2; it would go away once the snapshot is a Rust type.
The exit-code table comment was wrong (omitted clap's exit 2) and duplicated CLI-OUT-08 and docs/stability.md; replaced with a one-line pointer.
Orphaned doc lines about malformed PEP 440 parsing belonged to version.rs and were removed from a regression-test doc comment.

workflow: Verify sweep claims against the real binary and code before editing docs; earlier sweep claims have been wrong.
Apply the 'silent or costly failure' test before adding guards; loud, cheap, caught-before-shipping failures don't justify new CI machinery.
`gh pr close` has no comment-file option; post the comment with `gh pr comment --body-file`, then close.
Use `python3 -I` scripts with assert-on-anchor string substitution for safe multi-file doc edits.
Confirm before destructive or outward-facing actions (closing the PR and deleting the remote branch were done only after explicit user approval).

friction: The earlier #453 guard was built and then judged over-engineered, wasting effort and a PR.
Remote close/delete was previously blocked by the permission classifier, so the assistant had to be ready to hand over commands.
`gh pr close --comment-file` does not exist; first two attempts failed.
The sweep's claims were unreliable and each had to be verified individually.
Shell brittleness (gh_retry recursion, jq -e vs -r, set -e through command substitution, bash 3.2 vs 5, BSD vs GNU sed) consumed much of the session.
open_items: Open the docs-alignment PR (branch docs/align-with-code is pushed; PR body drafted in pr-docs.md) and link it to trail #237.
Delete the release-PR note feature from #431 (about 300 lines) as step 1 of the apply plan.

Implement `callisto release-pr apply` and `release-pr hold` in Rust per .claude/plans/DESIGN-release-pr-apply.md, starting with a read-only snapshot port and dry-run comparison against the shell output.
Then delete create-or-update-release-pr.sh, hold-release-pr.sh, gh_retry and the 615-line stub contract test once the Rust path is live.
Prune the remaining stub-only shell tests and trim install-callisto.sh (Windows .zip handling, crates.io fallback bypassing verification=require).
Remove the `--refresh-lockfiles` flag only after the workflow stops passing it.

Decide on the design questions: a callisto.toml [release-pr] table (recommended later), always draft a stale PR first (recommended yes), and ship the command and the switch in the same release (recommended yes).
Decide whether to keep the narration-cleanup grep guard (suggested only zero-false-positive patterns, or none) and investigate E248 as a possible silent wrong-version bug.
